text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ottawa to reopen cod fishery: Scientists condemn plan as political, see no clear sign number of fish is recovering.
- Deficit billions below target: C$16 billion hinted at.
- Fire in tent city kills hundreds: Many pilgrims trampled to death as Muslims flee blaze near Mecca.
- It's official: Quebec falls below 25 percent of population. Census adds to province's fears about influence in Canada.
- Albertans may get veto on taxes: Too easy to 'pick people's pockets' for revenue, Klein says.
- Nova profit surges 28 percent: Chemical division carries first-quarter results, but CEO rejects splitting up company.
- N.B. Tel poised to apply for cable TV licence: Firm awaits CRTC ruling on entering rival industry.
- De Guzman friend disputes suicide story: Bre-X employee describes geologist as 'happy' hours before his fatal fall.
- Placer Dome chief sees silver lining to Bre-X.
- Bulls charge back. Dow jumps 135.26 points, TSE up 64.22.
- Eaton's losing C$2 million a week as it rebuilds: Sales and inventories drop after flight into bankruptcy protection.
- Biochem stock reels on market criticism.
